problem.text: All three attention decode paths tested the truth value of q_norm_tensor instead of testing whether fused normalization weights were absent.

reasoning.text: Replacing `not self.q_norm_tensor` with `self.q_norm_tensor is None` makes dispatch depend on weight availability, not tensor contents.

impact.text: The correction covers uncached SDPA, uncached Flash Attention and cached Flash Attention. It removes the tensor truth-value evaluation before fused RMSNorm/RoPE without changing normalization parameters or backend calls.

source_notes.text: Read the QK LayerNorm ancestor entry, which identifies the tensor-truth dispatch regression and inherited native normalization/bounds concerns.

Issue #16, “RuntimeError: CUDA error: invalid configuration argument,” concerns conversion and a tokenizer-truncation diagnosis; #7, “quantizing model: undefined symbol: __cxa_call_terminate,” concerns extension loading; #29, “Auto-YaRN for Qwen3? Maybe even set it dynamically?”, concerns scaling policy. Their relationship here is inferred only from attention/rope path overlap, not evidence that this fix addresses those reports.

limitations: No PyTorch, CUDA kernel or model workflow was executed. The Python check models control flow with a truth-rejecting object; it does not reproduce PyTorch's exception.
Native numerical correctness and memory safety remain unverified by GPU execution. Literal caller searches do not establish dynamic or external reach.

chapters.title: Test fused normalization weights for absence

claims.text: Attention initializes normalization tensors to None and exposes loaded weights only for RMSNorm. LayerNorm therefore continues through separate Q/K normalization, while loaded RMSNorm with RoPE skips that fallback and passes its weights, epsilon and constant bias into RoPE.apply.

No-norm and no-RoPE short-circuit behavior is preserved. Standalone normalization still requests half output before rotation. RoPE.apply forwards optional weights to the native RMSNorm/rotation kernel, whose wrapper requires half Q/K and a one-dimensional Q normalization weight of head_dim elements.

A bounded Python control-flow transcription showed that a present truth-rejecting weight raises under the old condition but selects the fused route under the new condition. Missing weights, absent RoPE and absent normalization retained their branch results.

The ancestor's dispatch defect is removed by all three substitutions. Its native reduction and padded-read concerns are carried over: the task changes no native code, and successful dispatch alone does not establish correct fused-kernel execution.

findings.description: The newly reachable fused path retains conflicting shared reduction writes and unguarded padded input reads.
findings.trigger: Fused normalization with nonuniform lane values; or RoPE with a head width requiring padding, such as 80, or shorter partial-rotary frequencies.
findings.expected_behavior: Store one complete reduction per warp and restrict frequency and weight reads to their logical arrays.
findings.actual_behavior: Every lane writes its shuffle-down result to the same per-warp sums slot. inv_freq[t] and the normalization half2 weight read are unguarded. Attention's three decode methods reach RoPE.apply; the inspected science caller also invokes rotation but supplies no normalization weights.

verification.description: Compared native loads and reduction writes with the reduction helper, Python wrapper, attention callers and task diff.
verification.limits: No GPU race or memory-error reproduction.

verification.description: Launch arithmetic for head width 80 gives 64 x lanes but only 40 full-width frequency entries.
verification.limits: Python integer arithmetic only, not kernel execution.

annotation.summary: Corrects None checks across all attention backends, restoring dispatch to fused RMSNorm/RoPE while leaving inherited native-kernel concerns unchanged.
